outcomes.text: Use musical elements, techniques and resources to communicate ideas with technical and expressive control and a sense of style.
Perform with control and continuity at suitable tempi, showing understanding of the shape, direction and style of the piece.
Consider the purpose of the piece and the effect of audience, time and place.
Listen to established performers and appraise your own articulation, phrasing and dynamics.
Give a solo performance where your part plays a leading role, with the intended accompaniment.
Perform in an ensemble of two or more independent parts, attending to balance and the other players.
Improvise by learning the music accurately and then developing it, with attention to intonation, coherence and structure.
Realise music with technology, performing a live solo line with synthesisers, effects or loop pedals.
Perform from a score with accurate pitch, rhythm, tone and all directions, understanding the composer's intentions and context.
Rap with clear diction and breath control, or beatbox with varied timbres and rhythm control.
Perform from oral tradition or your own composition supported by a score.

subtopics.title: Elements, context and language in performing

outcomes.text: Apply organisation of pitch, tonality, structure, sonority, texture, tempo-metre-rhythm and dynamics in performing.
Read and use staff notation, chords and chord symbols, and musical vocabulary.
Create and develop musical ideas using elements, techniques and resources with technical control, freely or to a brief.
Use devices and conventions suited to the chosen genre, style and tradition.
Apply specialist vocabulary, notation and the link between compositional devices, harmony, tonality and structure.

subtopics.title: Writing for instruments, voices and technology

outcomes.text: Write idiomatically for instruments, voices or a digital audio workstation, handling timbre and texture.
Build ideas within forms and structures using sound harmonic, melodic and rhythmic construction.
Notate compositions using staff notation, graphic notation or written accounts.
Use sampling, synthesis, EQ, compression and effects in a DAW, blending samples with live instruments to create mood.

subtopics.title: Musical elements, contexts and language in composing

outcomes.text: Use the musical elements: pitch, tonality, structure, sonority, texture, tempo-metre-rhythm and dynamics.
Compose with attention to purpose, audience, time and place, and historical and cultural contexts.
Read and write staff notation including compound time and all key signatures, chords, inversions, seventh and extended chords.

topics.title: Briefs relating to areas of study

outcomes.text: Compose vocal music by studying song forms, word setting and accompaniments.
Compose instrumental music using instrument characteristics, ensembles and forms such as dance suite, sonata and string quartet.

subtopics.title: Film, fusion, popular and new directions briefs

outcomes.text: Compose film underscore that builds changing moods and atmospheres to dramatic action.
Compose fusions by combining harmony, melody, rhythm and instrumentation from different traditions.
Compose popular music and jazz using song structures, lead and backing textures and technology.
Compose new-directions music with atonality, tone rows and new timbres such as prepared instruments or electronics.
Write a free composition on any instrument or style, at least four minutes.
Harmonise a given chorale melody in Bach's style, adding alto, tenor and bass with correct voice-leading, modulation and suspensions.
Complete a two-part Baroque texture for bass and treble using stylish lines and 18th-century conventions.
Harmonise a given melody and extend it into an arrangement for up to four instruments or voices.
Develop an audio sample into a nightclub remix using electronic dance conventions, sample editing and sound manipulation, mixed clearly.
Analyse harmonic change, cadences, complex chord progressions such as secondary dominants, and melodic devices.
Explain key relationships including circle of fifths and enharmonic change.
Recognise structures such as sonata form, arch form, fugue and through-composed music.
Describe vocal timbres and instrumental techniques such as con sordino and sul ponticello.
Describe textures: monophony, homophony, polyphony, heterophony and fugue.
Identify metrical and rhythmic devices: changing metres, syncopation, additive rhythm, polyrhythm and swung rhythm.
Describe expressive use of dynamics and extreme ranges.
Explain how purpose, intention, audience, time and place shape how music is created and performed.
Explain how music from different periods and cultures has changed over time.
Read and write staff notation, chords and standard harmonic progressions, and use correct terminology.

subtopics.title: Aural skills, dictation and unfamiliar music

outcomes.text: Complete short melody, rhythm or chord dictation.
Listen perceptively to unfamiliar music to place it in genre, chronology and style, linking it to the set works.
Write evaluative essays comparing and judging music using musical vocabulary.
Analyse movements 1, 2 and 8 of Bach's Cantata Ein feste Burg, BWV 80, as a Baroque sacred work.
Analyse songs 1, 3 and 5 of On Wenlock Edge by Vaughan Williams as a 20th-century vocal work.
Analyse the first movement of Clara Wieck-Schumann's Piano Trio in G minor, Op. 17, as chamber music.
Analyse the first movement of Berlioz's programmatic Symphonie Fantastique.

topics.title: Area of study 3: Music for Film

outcomes.text: Analyse Danny Elfman's Batman Returns cues: Birth of a Penguin, Batman vs the Circus and The Rise and Fall from Grace.
Analyse Bernard Herrmann's Psycho cues from Prelude through Finale, including the shower scene.

topics.title: Area of study 4: Popular Music and Jazz

outcomes.text: Analyse Kate Bush's Cloudbusting, And dream of sheep and Under ice.
Analyse the Beatles' Eleanor Rigby, Here, there and everywhere, I want to tell you and Tomorrow never knows.

subtopics.title: Courtney Pine, Back in the Day

outcomes.text: Analyse Courtney Pine's Inner state (of mind), Lady Day and (John Coltrane), and Love and affection.
Analyse Pagodes and La soirée dans Grenade from Debussy's Estampes as a fusion of classical and other traditions.
Analyse Burn, Breathing Under Water and Easy by Anoushka Shankar as Indian-Western fusion.
Analyse Kaija Saariaho's Petals for cello and live electronics.
Analyse the Introduction, The Augurs of Spring and Ritual of Abduction from Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring.
